Cultural context: traditional gender roles ('machismo', 'the family first' norm that pressures women to stay in abusive marriages) create barriers to reporting. The Catholic Church's opposition to divorce means battered women must choose between unsafe marriages and expensive annulment.
laws.penalty: Physical violence against spouse/partner/child: up to 6 years imprisonment. Psychological violence (causing mental anguish): up to 12 years. Violation of Protection Order: 6-12 months.
exceptions: Safe houses operated by LGUs and NGOs provide temporary refuge for VAWC victims
Department of Social Welfare services must respond to VAWC cases within 24 hours
Victims have right to remain in the family home pending protection order enforcement

quiz.q: What makes the Philippines' VAWC Act distinctive in how it can provide immediate protection?
options: It allows police to arrest without a warrant for any VAWC complaint
Barangay Protection Orders may be issued same-day by village officials — providing immediate protection before a court order
All VAWC cases are heard within 24 hours in special family courts
Victims automatically receive government housing separate from the abuser
quiz.explanation: The Philippines' VAWC law is notable for enabling Barangay (village) Protection Orders issued by local barangay officials within the same day — much faster than court processes. Because the Philippines has 42,000+ barangays with officials present in every community, this creates a rapid first-response protection mechanism accessible even in remote areas without court infrastructure. The immediate BPO prohibits the abuser from approaching the victim; a court Temporary Protection Order follows within 72 hours.

laws.title: Republic Act 11057 — Personal Property Security Act
laws.subtitle: Business finance reform enabling asset-based lending
laws.fullDescription: The Philippines' Personal Property Security Act (2018) created a unified registry for security interests in movable property (equipment, accounts receivable, inventory) — enabling micro, small and medium businesses to use their assets as collateral for loans without land or building collateral. Before PPSA, Philippine banks primarily lent against real estate; MSMEs without property struggled to access credit. The Act implemented UNCITRAL Model Law recommendations. The Land Registration Authority operates the online collateral registry. This reform received recognition from the World Bank Doing Business project for improving credit access. The Philippines has a large small business sector that previously lacked access to formal credit.
laws.penalty: Fraudulent registration in Personal Property Security Registry: criminal prosecution for fraud. Unauthorized disposal of secured collateral: civil and potentially criminal liability.
exceptions: Agricultural assets in supervised credit programs under DA have modified registration requirements
Consumer credit for personal use below threshold exempt from PPSA registration
Aircraft and vessel mortgages governed by separate specialized statutes

quiz.q: What problem did the Philippines' Personal Property Security Act (2018) solve for small businesses?
options: It prevented large corporations from acquiring small businesses
It allowed businesses to use movable assets (equipment, receivables) as loan collateral — previously banks only accepted real estate, excluding most MSMEs
It created government-owned banks specifically for small business lending
It capped interest rates on small business loans at 5% annually
quiz.explanation: Philippine banks historically required real estate as collateral — excluding most MSMEs that lack land or buildings. The PPSA created a unified registry allowing security interests over movable property (equipment, inventory, accounts receivable, vehicles). This means a small restaurant can borrow against its equipment, or a micro-enterprise can use its livestock as collateral. The World Bank Doing Business report credited this reform with significantly improving access to credit in the Philippines.

laws.title: Republic Act 3019 — Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act
laws.subtitle: Philippine anti-corruption law and the Sandiganbayan
laws.fullDescription: The Philippines' Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act (1960) and the Sandiganbayan (special anti-graft court, 1978) are the primary instruments for prosecuting public official corruption. The Sandiganbayan handles cases against officials with salary grade 27 and above. The Office of the Ombudsman investigates and prosecutes government corruption. High-profile cases: former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo convicted of plunder (later acquitted by Supreme Court); Imelda Marcos convicted of 7 graft counts in 1993 (fled abroad, returned 1991). The 'Pork Barrel Scam' — legislators directing billions in public funds to fake NGOs — resulted in multiple senators' arrest. Estimated annual cost of government corruption: ₱700 billion.
laws.penalty: Graft/corruption: 6-15 years imprisonment. Plunder (amassing ill-gotten wealth through multiple acts): reclusion perpetua (40 years) without parole for amounts over ₱50M.
exceptions: Officials who turn state's witness and provide information on co-conspirators receive reduced charges
Restitution of corruptly obtained funds reduces charges in some plunder cases
Minor procedural violations distinguished from substantive graft

quiz.q: What is the Philippines' Sandiganbayan and what makes it unusual?
options: It is the Philippines' constitutional court for reviewing laws
A specialized court that exclusively handles corruption and graft cases against senior government officials — unusual in having a dedicated court for official corruption
It is a military tribunal for soldiers accused of extrajudicial killings
A special court for OFW-related legal disputes from overseas employment
quiz.explanation: The Sandiganbayan is a specialized anti-graft court created in 1978 with exclusive jurisdiction over criminal cases against public officials. Having a dedicated court — with specialized judges, prosecutors from the Ombudsman, and focus on public corruption — is unusual globally. The Sandiganbayan handles cases against officials at salary grade 27+ (mayors, senior civil servants, military officers), while the regular courts handle lower officials. Despite its existence, conviction rates and enforcement against powerful officials remain inconsistent.

laws.title: Republic Act 10591 — Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act
laws.subtitle: Philippine gun laws in a context of significant gun violence
laws.fullDescription: The Philippines' Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act (2013) regulates civilian firearms. The Philippines has relatively high civilian gun ownership for Asia (~5-7 per 100 people) — partly due to prolonged insurgencies, private security industry, and culture of personal protection. Licensed firearms require background checks, training, and registration. Gun bans during elections are imposed by COMELEC (Commission on Elections) — a unique provision where civilians cannot carry firearms during the election period to prevent political violence. The Philippines has significant gun violence including clan feuds (rido) in Mindanao and political killings. 'Loose firearms' (unlicensed guns) are widely available.
laws.penalty: Possession of unlicensed firearm: 4-10 years imprisonment. Carrying licensed firearm without permit to carry (outside home): 4-8 years. Violating COMELEC gun ban: 4-8 years.
exceptions: Police and military carry weapons under separate ordinances
Security agencies licensed by PNP may arm their guards
Licensed ROTC officers and sport shooters have modified carry permits

quiz.q: What unique electoral provision does the Philippines have regarding firearms?
options: Candidates must surrender their firearms for the duration of the campaign
COMELEC imposes a gun ban during election periods — civilians cannot carry firearms to prevent political violence
All firearms are confiscated by the government during election days
Polling station workers are armed by the military as election security
quiz.explanation: The Philippines' Commission on Elections (COMELEC) has authority to impose a 'gun ban' during election campaign and voting periods — typically prohibiting civilians (except authorized law enforcement) from carrying firearms. This is unique globally: a dedicated election authority with power to restrict constitutional rights to gun carrying during elections. The ban recognizes the Philippines' endemic problem of political violence, where electoral disputes have frequently turned violent with firearms.

laws.title: Republic Act 10654 — Fisheries Code
laws.subtitle: Managing the Philippines' waters amid illegal fishing and South China Sea tensions
laws.fullDescription: The Philippines' Fisheries Code (amended 2015 by RA 10654) governs fishing in Philippine waters. The Philippines has rich marine biodiversity — part of the Coral Triangle and among the world's top fish-consuming nations. Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated (IUU) fishing is a major challenge, particularly by Chinese vessels in Philippine EEZ. The 2016 South China Sea Arbitration Award (under UNCLOS) ruled in the Philippines' favor against China's nine-dash line, finding Chinese activities violated Philippine fishing rights. China rejected the ruling. Chinese coast guard confrontations with Filipino fishermen at Scarborough Shoal and Ayungin Shoal (BRP Sierra Madre) have escalated significantly under Marcos Jr. administration.
laws.penalty: Fishing without license in Philippine EEZ: vessel confiscation and fines up to ₱2M. Commercial fishing in municipal waters: up to 5 years and ₱2M fine. Illegal use of destructive fishing gear: up to 12 years.
exceptions: Municipal fisherfolk (3km coastal zone) have priority fishing rights over commercial vessels
Subsistence fishing by indigenous communities in ancestral waters recognized
Foreign vessels in transit under innocent passage rights — not allowed to fish
laws.sourceLabel: Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Philippines

quiz.q: What international legal victory did the Philippines win in 2016 regarding the South China Sea?
options: The Philippines won a military battle against China at Scarborough Shoal
The South China Sea Arbitration Award ruled in the Philippines' favor that China's nine-dash line claim violated UNCLOS — China rejected the ruling
The UN General Assembly voted to recognize the Philippines' maritime claims
The US Seventh Fleet formally guaranteed Philippine sovereignty over its EEZ
quiz.explanation: In July 2016, an international arbitration tribunal under UNCLOS issued a landmark ruling in the Philippines v. China case: China's nine-dash line claim was incompatible with UNCLOS, Chinese artificial islands were built on Philippine EEZ areas, and China had violated Philippine fishing and resource rights. It was the most definitive legal ruling on South China Sea claims. China immediately rejected the ruling as 'null and void' and has not complied with it — but it remains the authoritative statement of international law on the dispute.

laws.title: Republic Act 11054 — Bangsamoro Organic Law
laws.subtitle: Peace process and autonomy for Muslim Mindanao
laws.fullDescription: The Philippines' Bangsamoro Organic Law (BOL, 2018) established the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), replacing the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM). The BOL was the legislative realization of decades of peace negotiations with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) — ending a conflict that killed 120,000+ since the 1970s. BARMM has its own parliament (Bangsamoro Parliament), government structure, Sharia court system, and Bangsamoro Islamic Criminal Code jurisdiction over Muslim personal matters. Block grants from Manila are significant. Implementation has been complex: smaller splinter groups (BIFF, Abu Sayyaf) continue armed activities; disarmament of MILF forces proceeding slowly.
laws.penalty: Crimes in BARMM may be tried under national criminal law or Bangsamoro Islamic Criminal Code for applicable Muslim personal matters. Abu Sayyaf activities: counter-terrorism law applies.
exceptions: Non-Muslims in BARMM are not subject to Sharia personal law
National laws on natural resources, foreign investment, and criminal offenses apply throughout BARMM
Traditional indigenous people's (Lumad) rights recognized alongside Bangsamoro rights
laws.sourceLabel: Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao

quiz.q: What decades-long conflict did the Bangsamoro Organic Law (2018) help resolve?
options: A communist New People's Army insurgency in Muslim Mindanao
The Moro conflict — a separatist insurgency by Muslim Filipinos against the Manila government since the 1970s, killing 120,000+
A dispute between the Philippines and Malaysia over Sabah
A territorial dispute with Indonesia over the Sulu Archipelago
quiz.explanation: The Moro conflict in Mindanao — primarily between the Philippine government and Moro (Muslim Filipino) separatist movements (MNLF, MILF, and others) — has been one of Southeast Asia's longest insurgencies. It killed 120,000+ people and displaced millions since the 1970s, motivated by Moro Muslim identity and historical injustice from Christian Filipino migration into Muslim ancestral lands. The Bangsamoro Organic Law implemented the 2014 peace agreement with the MILF, creating genuine autonomy rather than the failed ARMM predecessor.
